children: Aerospace and defense tech firm's Q3 revenue rose 179% yr/yr, beating analyst expectations
Gross margin improved to 57% from 44%, driven by higher drone sales and efficiencies
Company expects full-yr 2026 revenue growth at lower end of 15%-25% range
Company expects 2026 revenue growth at the lower end of 15%-25% range
Company reiterates 2026 adjusted EBITDA guidance in negative mid- to high-teens mln-dollar range
AIRO expects majority of $200 mln drone backlog to convert to revenue in next 12 months
DRONES SEGMENT - Revenue growth was driven by stronger performance in the Drones segment, partially offset by softness in Avionics and Training businesses
GROSS MARGIN EXPANSION - Gross margin rose due to a favorable mix shift toward higher-volume drone sales and improved operating efficiencies
HIGHER OPERATING EXPENSES - Profitability was impacted by increased operating expenses tied to investments to scale the business and support long-term growth objectives
The current average analyst rating on the shares is "buy" and the breakdown of recommendations is 3 "strong buy" or "buy", 1 "hold" and no "sell" or "strong sell"
The average consensus recommendation for the aerospace & defense peer group is "buy"
Wall Street's median 12-month price target for AIRO Group Holdings Inc is $16.00, about 193% above its November 11 closing price of $5.46
